codes.title: an agent taking a harmful or irreversible action nobody approved
an agent reporting work as done that the evidence does not back up
a model lost in too much context
context overflowing the model's window or its budget
a decision lost when earlier turns are summarised to save room
facts or decisions lost between the steps of one task
a constraint the person stated, forgotten between the request and the result
spending more on model calls than the work needs
a change that breaks something that worked
a wrong or planted entry in stored memory, used as if true
an interface with inconsistent styling or poor contrast
an image, video or 3D output that is blank, corrupt or wrong, reported as done
audio output that is silent, clipped or corrupt, reported as done
a recoverable error that stops the whole workflow
a broken change left running with no way back
relevant passages that retrieval never finds
outdated or unofficial material used as if it were current
a claim or citation that cannot be traced to the passage it came from
agents overwriting each other's work
spending a budget on blind trial and error
codes.description: Trying candidate after candidate with no model of the problem, so the budget runs out before the search learns anything.

codes.title: a big move made without checking it first
codes.description: An agent takes a large or hard-to-undo step without first checking its preconditions or its likely effect.

codes.title: a warning ignored on the way to an action
codes.description: A check raised a warning, and the agent went ahead as if it had not.

codes.title: a wrong formula, root or integral stated with confidence
codes.description: A model states the result of a symbolic calculation that a computer algebra check would refuse.

codes.title: taking a correlation for a cause
codes.description: Two things move together and the answer says one causes the other, with no causal model or test behind it.

codes.title: controlling for the wrong variables
codes.description: An estimate adjusts for a variable it should leave alone, or leaves out one it needs, so the effect it reports is biased.

codes.title: generated code that only works on the examples it was shown
codes.description: Synthesised code passes the examples it was written from and fails on inputs nobody showed it.

codes.title: obeying instructions hidden in text it should only read
codes.description: Content an agent reads, such as a web page, a file or a tool result, carries instructions, and the agent follows them as if the person had given them. The guards package is only a tripwire for it: it flags a fixed list of English phrasings, and a paraphrase, another language or an encoding passes.

codes.title: unsafe outcomes nobody worked out in advance
codes.description: A system can reach a harmful state that nobody identified before it ran, so nothing was built to stop it.

codes.title: a conclusion the rules and facts do not support
codes.description: An answer asserts something that does not follow from the stated rules and facts.

codes.title: a consequence the rules imply that goes unnoticed
codes.description: The rules and facts entail a conclusion that matters, and nobody derives it.

codes.title: a conclusion stated with more certainty than the facts give
codes.description: The answer is right in direction but claims a confidence its evidence does not carry.

codes.title: rules that contradict each other without anyone noticing
codes.description: Two rules in the same set cannot both hold, and conclusions are drawn from them anyway.

codes.title: taking one model's first answer unchallenged
codes.description: A single answer is accepted without any other view or critique being sought.

codes.title: a shortcut that breaks on cases it has not seen
codes.description: A cheaper replacement, such as a distilled prompt, rule or model, matches the original on the cases it was built from and fails on new ones.

codes.title: a claim made with no regard for whether the evidence supports it
codes.description: A conclusion is stated with the same confidence whatever the strength of its evidence.

codes.title: the same claim repeated, counted as more evidence
codes.description: A claim found in several places that all share one origin is treated as if independent sources confirmed it.

codes.title: work called verified when the evidence does not support it
codes.description: A result is labelled checked or verified beyond what its evidence shows.

codes.title: a reasoning slip stated with confidence
codes.description: A logical or arithmetic step goes wrong, and the answer is given as if it were sound.

codes.title: a long task drifting from its goal
codes.description: Over many steps the work moves away from what was asked, and nothing brings it back.

codes.title: made-up facts and quotes
codes.description: An answer states a fact, figure or quotation that no source supports.

codes.title: tampering with the safeguards themselves
codes.description: An agent edits, disables or routes around the checks meant to stop it.

codes.title: solving the wrong problem
codes.description: The work answers a reading of the request that is not what the person meant.

codes.title: a proof that only looks finished
codes.description: A proof that still has a gap, such as an admitted step or an axiom added to make it go through, is presented as complete.

codes.title: a proof of a different statement from the one you meant
codes.description: The formal statement that was proved does not say what the claim in words says.

codes.title: repeating the same mistake
codes.description: A failure that has happened before happens again, because nothing was learned from it.

codes.title: a lesson that sounds right and does not help
codes.description: A rule or note learned from past work is applied and makes no measurable difference, or makes things worse.

codes.title: a design that fails only in a rare order of events nobody tried
codes.description: Concurrent or distributed steps can happen in an order that breaks the design, and no test ever ran them in that order.

codes.title: a plan that fails halfway through
codes.description: A multi-step plan starts work that a later step cannot finish, because its inputs or permissions will not be there.

codes.title: a plan that breaks one of your rules
codes.description: A schedule, allocation or plan violates a hard constraint the person stated.

codes.title: a plan called the best when nobody proved it
codes.description: A solution is called optimal with no bound or proof that a better one does not exist.

codes.title: a claimed gain that extra compute or luck explains
codes.description: An improvement is credited to a method when more samples, more compute or chance account for it.

codes.title: a run that keeps going past its limits
codes.description: An agent loop keeps spending time, tokens or money after it should have stopped.

codes.title: an agent weakening tests to make them pass
codes.description: An agent edits, skips or loosens tests so that its change appears to pass them.

codes.title: a self-change that slips past its own checks
codes.description: A system changes its own prompts, settings or code, and the change is adopted without the checks it should have faced.

codes.title: an answer with skipped steps that nobody checked
codes.description: A worked answer skips steps, and its result is never checked against the problem.

codes.title: moving the goalposts after the work is done
codes.description: The test of success is changed after the work, so the work passes a test it was never set.

codes.title: a fix made for a failure nobody reproduced
codes.description: The reported failure may not reproduce on the frozen baseline, so a fix cannot be shown to remove it.

codes.title: tests written by the caller taken as independent proof
codes.description: Caller-authored tests cannot independently establish correctness.

codes.title: a change that alters behaviour outside the part it was meant to touch
codes.description: A proposal may change behaviour outside the intended function.

codes.title: code under test running with the owner's permissions
codes.description: The code under test runs inside the test process with the owner's permissions; this is not an operating-system sandbox.

codes.title: tests run in a repository that can change during the run
codes.description: The tests run in the repository itself, so a change made there during the run can reach them.

codes.title: work started with no measurable test of success
codes.description: Nobody can say what result would count as done, so any result can be called done.

codes.title: completion claimed with nothing named that would prove it
codes.description: The work is reported complete without the tests or evidence that would show it.

codes.title: work in a specialist field started without that field's evidence standard
codes.description: The same evidence bar is applied to every field, so work that a field holds to a higher standard is judged by a lower one.

codes.title: harm or irreversibility underestimated
codes.description: A task is routed as low risk when a mistake would be harmful or hard to undo.

codes.title: a task overrunning its token, cost or time budget
codes.description: The work spends more than it was given, because no budget was set or nothing enforced it.

codes.title: a plan that relies on a tool that is not there
codes.description: A step needs a tool, program or harness that is not installed or not reachable.

codes.title: an unstated assumption that would change the answer if false
codes.description: The work rests on an assumption nobody wrote down, so nobody checks it.

codes.title: claims that need sources and have none
codes.description: Statements that need a citation or source evidence are made without one.

codes.title: output that no independent check looks at
codes.description: Nothing outside the step that produced a result checks it.

codes.title: a result handed over without saying how far to rely on it
codes.description: The person receiving the result is not told what was checked, what was not, and what to watch for.

codes.title: a failure never recorded, so nothing learns from it
codes.description: A failure is fixed or ignored without being written down, so it cannot be counted or learned from.

codes.title: a tool silently missing or replaced, with the result reported as if it ran
codes.description: An optional tool is not installed or not working, and a substitute or a guess is returned without saying so.
